observations: Linux logs Run /init as init process.
The only visible unprefixed userspace output is literal D immediately before the ACPI S5 preparation log.
Host runner independently observes powered-off, but records no guest userspace receipt and returns exit1.
diagnosis: UART source review found no transmit-empty interrupt implementation; Linux identifies the port as16450, whose interrupt-driven transmitter writes one byte per service. This explains the observed prefix while polling printk is intact. A UART correction and later reboot are outside this receipt.
observationScope: Last runner slice exits; guest-handled exceptions are not sampled. Timeout state is the last completed slice.
limitations: Poweroff alone does not prove workload completion. The guest could have taken an early error/shutdown branch; the missing serial receipt leaves workload results unknown.
No exact fault state is inferred from CR2 or previous completed slice state. Guest-handled exceptions are not sampled.
This baseline-JIT musl probe does not provide glibc, interpreter-equivalence, systemd, stress or physical-machine qualification.
